:::{#rem-real-coordinate-space-notation}
#### Reading $\vx \in \reals^p$

Writing $\vx \in \reals^p$ says, in one symbol,
that $\vx$ is a column vector with $p$ real entries.
For example, $(1, -2, 0.5) \in \reals^3$.
The vector $(1, 2)$ is not in $\reals^3$, because it has only $2$ entries;
it is in $\reals^2$.
In @exr-list-as-vector, $\vx \in \reals^3$.

:::
